title: Transactional EKS control plane Terraform provisioner with preflight validation and proactive heal checks
creator: Ava Lin
description: Implement a transactional Terraform-based provisioner for Redwood Private EKS control planes that ensures idempotent, observable, and self-healing provisioning flows. The module should provide: (1) preflight schema & quota validation; (2) a transactional apply wrapper that safely sequences resource creation and can roll back or mark a failed state for automated remediation; (3) built-in health checks and periodic probes for control plane components (API server, etcd snapshot/restore readiness, certificate expiry); (4) explicit upgrade hooks that run pre/post validation and capture telemetry; (5) clear observability outputs for Console (events, metrics, traces). The goal is to reduce manual intervention during initial cluster bootstrap and upgrades, improve upgrade safety, and enable automated recovery for common provisioning failure modes.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes a single composable module (redwood_priv_eks_controlplane) with documented inputs/outputs
Module runs idempotently: repeated apply leaves cluster in desired state without resource thrash
Preflight checks fail fast with actionable messages when quotas, IAM roles, or KMS keys are missing
Transactional wrapper supports marking runs as FAILED and emits diagnosis bundle to S3 for later replay
Health checks detect and emit metrics for API server latency, unreachable etcd, and kubelet certificate expiry
Upgrade flow supports canary apply to 5% of control planes and automatic rollback on health regression metric
End-to-end test harness exists in CI that provisions a sandbox control plane and validates health probes and rollback behavior
tasks: Design: finalize module interface and required outputs (inputs: cluster_name, private_subnets, kms_key_arn, control_plane_size)
Implement: terraform module resources (EKS control plane, IAM roles, KMS bindings, node bootstrap SRs)
Implement: transactional controller wrapper (lambda/statemachine) that sequences plan->apply and handles rollbacks
Implement: preflight checks (quota, IAM, KMS, VPC constraints) with deterministic errors
Implement: health probe collection (Prometheus exporter + CloudWatch metrics) and Console integration
Write: CI integration tests (sandbox provisioning, deliberate failure injection, rollback validation)
Docs: Confluence module spec and runbook for operators
Rollout: staged enablement and monitoring for Dedicated and Private customers

notes: Trade-offs considered: terraform-operator approach was rejected because it made rollback semantics opaque; a controller/statemachine that orchestrates plain terraform CLI runs preserves clearer plan/apply audit trail. We will keep the module API small and push orchestration into a thin service so operators can reuse the same module in CI, console-driven provisioning, or a one-off tenant bootstraper. Rollback strategy will favor leave-and-repair (emit diagnosis, mark FAILED) rather than automatic destructive rollback for multi-tenant safety.
